F1 schedule: When is the next race and where is it being held?
Starts in Mexico City can often get interesting.
The F1 schedule is now heading towards the closing stages for the 2026 season, as the grid looks to decide how the year pans out.
The sport had been reduced to a 22-race schedule after two cancellations and, while the Bahrain Grand Prix was reinstated in Malaysia, a decision has yet to be taken about confirmation that scheduled rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will still go ahead.
Which race is next on the F1 schedule?
Round 19: Mexico City Grand Prix
The Mexico City Grand Prix sees a thrilling atmosphere gather in Mexico’s capital as the fans in attendance will have a home hero to cheer on once again, with Sergio Perez having returned to the grid in 2026.
Taking place on the weekend prior to Dia de los Muertos [Day of the Dead], Formula 1 will join the celebrations as the now-iconic Foro Sol Stadium will play host to tens of thousands of fans, each with a view of the podium on race day.
The high altitude and long pit straight combine to produce the highest top speeds of the season in Formula 1, with less air resistance meaning the cars can go even faster than usual.
The F1 2026 season has very much turned towards its home straight, and there is a huge amount still to be decided on the grid.
When is the Mexico City Grand Prix?
The Mexico City Grand Prix will take place from Friday 30 October until Sunday 1 November, with the race starting at 2pm local time [8pm UK] on Sunday 1 November.
What records are in progress during the F1 season?
F1 race wins: Which drivers have the highest win totals in F1 history?
F1 points all-time rankings: Where do Hamilton, Verstappen and Alonso feature?
Where is the Mexico City Grand Prix?
The Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez is a 4.304km circuit which combines massive top speeds on the pit straight, as well as tricky technical corners which bring the circuit together.
The huge run down to Turn 1 is among the longest of the season, meaning it is a drag race to start as well as possible, and the left-right-left combination to open a lap leads onto another straight which offers another overtaking opportunity into Turn 4.
A tricky, slow double-right follows before the drivers buid up speed towards the fast sweeps of Turns 7 through to 11.
Another short straight follows before hitting the brakes and turning right into the Foro Sol section, with the drivers intersecting among the fans to finish the lap, with the final right-hander catapulting the drivers back onto the pit straight.
Is the Mexico City Grand Prix an F1 Sprint weekend?
No, the Mexico City Grand Prix is not an F1 Sprint weekend.
This means the drivers will have two free practice sessions on race weekend Friday, followed by FP3 and qualifying on Saturday, with the race taking place on Sunday.
All six Sprints for the 2026 season have now taken place.

FP3: 11.30am-12.30pm [5.30pm-6.30pm UK] Qualifying: 3pm-4pm [9pm-10pm UK]
Mexico City Grand Prix: 2pm [8pm UK] [71 laps]

F1 2026 schedule: Full race calendar, round dates for Formula One season
There's no shortage of excitement surrounding the 2026 Formula 1 campaign.
This season includes a raft of new regulations relating to engines, chassis, tyres and fuel, which could make for some unpredictable races between now and the end of the year.
Lando Norris became world champion for the first time in 2025 after finishing third at a dramatic concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, edging out race winner Max Verstappen in the title battle by just two points. McLaren and Red Bull were expected to lead the charge again, although Mercedes ' pace early in the season meant they were the team to beat.
The Sporting News has the full schedule for 2026.
MORE: Which driver has the most wins in F1 history?
F1 schedule 2026
The 2026 F1 season was again due to feature 24 races, but the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia Grands Prix were cancelled because of the war in the Middle East. The Bahrain race was officially staged in Malaysia in October.
There is also a slight change to the lineup for this year.
The Spanish Grand Prix, which will be held in September, has been relocated to a new Madrid street circuit. That means the race in Barcelona will now be called the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, which will take place in June.
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku has been moved to a Saturday to avoid a clash with the national day of remembrance.
The season began at Albert Park in Australia, with the Chinese Grand Prix then kicking off a run of four races in Asia, as was the case in 2025.
Miami followed before the action headed to Europe in June, beginning with the Monaco Grand Prix on June 7. All races will then be held in that continent until October.
Azerbaijan and Singapore are next on the schedule before F1 heads to the Americas, with Grands Prix to be held in the United States (Las Vegas and Austin), Mexico and Brazil.
The last two races of the season will take place in the Middle East, with Abu Dhabi to host the finale, as usual.
Bahrain, Saudi Arabia Grands Prix cancelled
F1 organisers chose to cancel the races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia because of the conflict in the Middle East that began with the United States and Israel's attack on Iran.
The event in Bahrain was due to take place over the weekend of April 10-12, with the season heading to Jeddah a week later.
The races were cancelled rather than postponed, so rather than have them rescheduled or replaced, the season has been shortened to 22 races.
F1 2026 sprint race schedule
Three of the six sprint venues for 2026 will host these shortened races for the first time.
The first sprint once more took place in the second race weekend of the season in Shanghai. The next was in Miami in early May.
Montreal then hosted its first sprint at the end of that month, with the Dutch and Singapore Grands Prix also staging the race for the first time, after Silverstone in July.

Where to watch the Formula 1 MSC Cruises United States Grand Prix 2026
Fans in the United States can watch the Formula 1 MSC Cruises United States Grand Prix 2026 and every race this season live on Apple TV , the exclusive home of F1 in the US.
For the 2026 season, Apple TV will host all Free Practice, Qualifying, Sprint sessions, and Grands Prix with select races and all Free Practice sessions throughout the season available to watch for free in the Apple TV app.
New subscribers to Apple TV can sign up for a 7-day FREE trial . After that, the subscription will cost $14.99/month.
F1 2026 driver lineup, grid
New on the grid this year are Audi and Cadillac, the former having taken the place and drivers of Sauber.
Cadillac line up with veteran drivers Sergio Perez, formerly of Red Bull, and Valtteri Bottas, twice a world championship runner-up with Mercedes.

F1 2026 schedule: Full race calendar, round dates for Formula One season
There's no shortage of excitement surrounding the 2026 Formula 1 campaign.
This season includes a raft of new regulations relating to engines, chassis, tyres and fuel, which could make for some unpredictable races between now and the end of the year.
Lando Norris became world champion for the first time in 2025 after finishing third at a dramatic concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix, edging out race winner Max Verstappen in the title battle by just two points. McLaren and Red Bull were expected to lead the charge again, although Mercedes ' pace early in the season meant they were the team to beat.
The Sporting News has the full schedule for 2026.
MORE: Which driver has the most wins in F1 history?
F1 schedule 2026
The 2026 F1 season was again due to feature 24 races, but the Bahrain and Saudi Arabia Grands Prix were cancelled because of the war in the Middle East. The Bahrain race was officially staged in Malaysia in October.
There is also a slight change to the lineup for this year.
The Spanish Grand Prix, which will be held in September, has been relocated to a new Madrid street circuit. That means the race in Barcelona will now be called the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix, which will take place in June.
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku has been moved to a Saturday to avoid a clash with the national day of remembrance.
The season began at Albert Park in Australia, with the Chinese Grand Prix then kicking off a run of four races in Asia, as was the case in 2025.
Miami followed before the action headed to Europe in June, beginning with the Monaco Grand Prix on June 7. All races will then be held in that continent until October.
Azerbaijan and Singapore are next on the schedule before F1 heads to the Americas, with Grands Prix to be held in the United States (Las Vegas and Austin), Mexico and Brazil.
The last two races of the season will take place in the Middle East, with Abu Dhabi to host the finale, as usual.
Bahrain, Saudi Arabia Grands Prix cancelled
F1 organisers chose to cancel the races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia because of the conflict in the Middle East that began with the United States and Israel's attack on Iran.
The event in Bahrain was due to take place over the weekend of April 10-12, with the season heading to Jeddah a week later.
The races were cancelled rather than postponed, so rather than have them rescheduled or replaced, the season has been shortened to 22 races.
F1 2026 sprint race schedule
Three of the six sprint venues for 2026 will host these shortened races for the first time.
The first sprint once more took place in the second race weekend of the season in Shanghai. The next was in Miami in early May.
Montreal then hosted its first sprint at the end of that month, with the Dutch and Singapore Grands Prix also staging the race for the first time, after Silverstone in July.

Fans in the United States can watch the Formula 1 MSC Cruises United States Grand Prix 2026 and every race this season live on Apple TV , the exclusive home of F1 in the US.
For the 2026 season, Apple TV will host all Free Practice, Qualifying, Sprint sessions, and Grands Prix with select races and all Free Practice sessions throughout the season available to watch for free in the Apple TV app.
New subscribers to Apple TV can sign up for a 7-day FREE trial . After that, the subscription will cost $14.99/month.
F1 2026 driver lineup, grid
New on the grid this year are Audi and Cadillac, the former having taken the place and drivers of Sauber.
Cadillac line up with veteran drivers Sergio Perez, formerly of Red Bull, and Valtteri Bottas, twice a world championship runner-up with Mercedes.
The big change near the top of the field sees Isack Hadjar take over as Red Bull's teammate for Max Verstappen. British driver Arvid Lindblad replaces Hadjar at Racing Bulls for his debut year.
